content.text: I found the single poisonous release: `@lightdash/cli@0.103.0-alpha.9` publishes the legacy field as `bundleDependencies: [true]`. The current release is clean, but mise fetches and deserializes the full version history, so that one malformed 2022 entry prevents resolving today’s `latest`. I’m checking how npm treated that tarball so the upstream fix doesn’t guess at `[true]` semantics.

content.text:
Confirmed: the user’s `mise.toml` is correct. This is an upstream aube parsing bug exposed by mise.

The npm registry contains one malformed historical release, `@lightdash/cli@0.103.0-alpha.9` from 2022:

```json
"bundleDependencies": [true]
```

npm defines this field as either a boolean or an array of package-name strings—not an array containing a boolean. Registry metadata historically wasn’t strongly validated, so malformed records exist. [npm package.json documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/files/package.json/#bundledependencies), [npm registry documentation](https://github.com/npm/registry/blob/master/docs/responses/package-metadata.md).

mise fetches the package’s complete version history for timestamps and deprecation filtering in [npm_registry.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/5eb9/mise/src/backend/npm_registry.rs:63). Embedded aube deserializes every version using `Vec<String> | bool`; the old `[true]` record therefore aborts the entire response before mise can resolve the clean current `latest` release. This exactly reproduces the [Discussion #13007](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13007) error.

Immediate workaround:

```toml
[settings.npm]
shell_out = true

[tools]
node = "latest"
"npm:@lightdash/cli" = "latest"
```

Or temporarily:

```sh
MISE_NPM_SHELL_OUT=1 mise install
```

I verified that this makes `mise ls-remote npm:@lightdash/cli` succeed. Setting only `npm.package_manager = "npm"` is insufficient because metadata lookup still uses aube unless `npm.shell_out` is enabled.

The proper fix belongs in `aubepkg/aube`: tolerate invalid entries inside `bundleDependencies` arrays, retaining strings and ignoring other values. For this release, `[true]` should become an empty list; its published tarball contains no bundled `node_modules` entries. Then mise should update `aube` and `aube-registry` together. No workspace changes were made.

I’ll fix this in `aubepkg/aube`, where the strict manifest parser lives, add regression coverage for the exact Lightdash payload, run aube’s focused checks, then open a ready-for-review upstream PR. Afterward I’ll determine whether mise also needs a dependency-bump PR or whether that should wait for an aube release.

content.text:
CI is failing before compiling our code. Both native matrices hit:

```text
mise ERROR "mbx" couldn't exec process: No such file or directory
```

The causal chain:

1. The workflows set `install: false`, so `mr-boxington`/`mbx` is not installed.
2. They run `mise exec -- cargo build …`.
3. aube’s `mise.toml` wraps Cargo with `command = "mbx"`.
4. mise 2026.9.3 now activates command wrappers under `mise exec`, following [mise #12908](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12908).
5. `MBX_DISABLE=1` configures mbx after launch; it cannot help when the `mbx` executable is missing.

That explains why every Linux/macOS FFI and Node-addon target failed identically: [FFI job](https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/actions/runs/34362281995/job/102502070973), [Node-addon job](https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/actions/runs/34362282112/job/102502065775).

This is unrelated to the parser change. The previous successful workflow used mise 2026.9.1; this run automatically picked up 2026.9.3. The clean fix is likely to use plain `cargo build` in these `install: false` jobs, as their release branches already do, or explicitly install mbx.
